stem: Find the sum $\frac{1}{{=m}\times{=m+1}}+\frac{1}{{=m+1}\times{=m+2}}+\frac{1}{{=m+2}\times{=m+3}}+\dots+\frac{1}{{=n}\times{=n+1}}$. Give the answer as a fraction in its simplest form, written a/b.
solution: Cancel the terms that add to zero; what remains is $\frac{1}{{=m}}-\frac{1}{{=n+1}}$.
$\frac{1}{{=m}}-\frac{1}{{=n+1}}=\frac{{=num}}{{=den}}$, which in simplest form is $\frac{{=num // g}}{{=den // g}}$.
notes: Basic entry: unit-difference partial fractions 1/(k(k+1)), numeric start m (1-4) and end n; answer = 1/m - 1/(n+1) reduced. num<den always so answer is never a whole number. Answer string a/b matches book style (e.g. 1425/1984).
